title: SolarPunk Energy Standard Economics
one_line: SolarPunk is an energy-standard cryptocurrency: a modern gold-standard system where verified renewable-energy surplus replaces gold as the backing base.
thesis: SPK supply should expand only when productive energy surplus is measured, admitted, signed, and converted through a transparent issuance rule.

monetary_equations.fee_capture: protocol_currency_fee = mint_fee_spk + redemption_fee_spk; settlement transfers currently have no protocol fee in SolarPunkCurrencySystem

empirical_foundation.interpretation: The thesis evidence motivates energy as an economically meaningful crypto variable; it does not by itself prove SPK demand or legal currency status.

solar_resource_basis.cost_basis_boundary: This is a sizing assumption from the resource benchmark, not a vendor quote or investment-return promise.

gold_standard_mapping.implementation: signed meter/inverter data, source hashes, oracle attestation, replay protection
gold_standard_mapping.remaining_risk: meter custody, data quality, basis mismatch, and operator honesty

gold_standard_mapping.implementation: meter registry, accepted bundle, consumed source hash, accepted kWh
gold_standard_mapping.remaining_risk: hardware certification and no-double-counting registry discipline
legal redemption terms and real delivery counterparty

gold_standard_mapping.implementation: mintFromSurplusAttestation accepts only admissible surplus evidence
gold_standard_mapping.remaining_risk: governance must not weaken admissibility rules

monetary_function_readiness.evidence: SPK mints from signed surplus attestation with source-hash replay protection.
Prototype uses a USD/kWh basis; the deeper energy standard is kWh-per-SPK convertibility.
SolarPunkCurrencySystem settles hashed invoices in SPK locally.
Needs real redemption terms, liquidity, governance, audit, and user demand.
Redemption receipts can record owed kWh with fulfillment, shortfall, and dispute states.
Energy evidence and public readback exist; production-grade registry, audit, and operator controls are still open.

finance_risk_register.meaning: A generic kWh estimate is not always deliverable where and when the holder needs energy.
Bad hardware, bad signatures, duplicate claims, or compromised operators can corrupt issuance.
finance_risk_register.control: Hardware-backed meters, no-double-counting registry, multi-oracle checks, and slashing.

finance_risk_register.meaning: Issued SPK may circulate faster or farther than the operator's real delivery ability.
finance_risk_register.control: Caps, redemption queues, insurance fund, shortfall rules, and local delivery domains.

finance_risk_register.meaning: Changing USD/kWh basis changes issuance volume and kWh-per-SPK convertibility.
finance_risk_register.control: Transparent governance delay, public parameter history, and basis-policy disclosure.

finance_risk_register.meaning: SPK could be treated as prepaid energy credit, commodity receipt, stablecoin-like token, security, or another instrument.

hard_boundaries: This is an economic framework and sensitivity model, not a claim of legal money status.
The protocol does not create energy; it creates an issuance rule over verified productive energy surplus.
NASA/resource estimates can size the backing base, but cannot mint SPK.
The current redemption loop is local/lab evidence unless a real operator accepts the obligation.
The same-cost capex sensitivity is not a vendor quote, project-finance model, or expected return promise.
next_finance_build_targets: Add time/location/vintage tags to SPK issuance and redemption receipts.
Build a monetary stress harness for redemption waves, velocity spikes, oracle errors, and shortfalls.
Define an explicit reserve/insurance fund policy tied to outstanding owed-kWh exposure.
Write a legally cautious redemption policy for pilot operators.
Replace the resource benchmark with one real generator export and rerun the same issuance model.
